podcast.body: "Radioactive" by Imagine Dragons was the third best-selling digital track of the 2010s, with 8.5 million sales. This demonstrated significant commercial success for a rock-leaning track in a decade dominated by pop and hip hop in digital sales. "The third best selling digital track of the 2010s, Imagine Dragons and Radioactive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 5: Music and Tech

podcast.body: The first track from the `Continued Silence` EP, inspired by Dan Reynolds losing his faith in Mormonism. It was a major hit, staying on the singles charts for a then-record 87 weeks and selling 3 million copies, making it one of the biggest-selling rock songs in history according to Soundscan. It also won a Grammy for Best Rock Performance. "A song inspired by when Dan Reynolds lost his faith in Mormonism."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The success of Imagine Dragons' "Radioactive" created an "open lane" in the music industry, which USS also benefited from with their dubstep-infused rock song "This Is The Best," as both songs found momentum simultaneously. "That was also when I imagined dragons when radio active had kicked off. So it was almost like we had a similar experience."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
